a4e52f3e2473b5e18b05be0dcde2019164f0c48e.summary: Quorum Cyber describes SharpRhino, a C# remote access trojan (RAT) it found during a ransomware incident it investigated. The malware is delivered through typosquatting that impersonates the Angry IP Scanner tool, establishes persistence on execution, and gives the attacker remote access. Quorum Cyber attributes the incident to Hunters International, a ransomware-as-a-service group, and says the malware variant is linked to the ThunderShell malware family.

hedges: It is highly likely that this is the first time Hunters International has been reported deploying this Remote Access Trojan (RAT), based on there being no indicators of previous use.
Attribution to Hunters International rests on TTPs observed during the investigation and identification within the ransom note itself.

It describes helpdesk and insider social engineering, OAuth token abuse against SaaS platforms, and double extortion. Cited victims include Red Hat GitLab and LVMH/Gucci. A possible Iranian link is hedged as unconfirmed. Figures come from other vendors.
